options.text: Walter Christaller, in 1933: all cities are identical in size
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Von Thunen, in 1826: cities are concentric rings of wheat
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Mark Jefferson, in 1939: the largest city in a nation being disproportionately larger than any other (often twice as large as the second city)
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT principle for Urban Hierarchy Theories.

options.text: August Losch, in 1940: hexagonal markets across an isotropic plain
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for India: People and Economy - Population & Settlements (Urban Hierarchy Theories):
Mark Jefferson, in 1939: the largest city in a nation being disproportionately larger than any other (often twice as large as the second city)

Detailed Analysis:
The Law of the Primate City was formulated by Mark Jefferson in 1939, asserting that a country's leading city is disproportionately large and exceptionally expressive of national capacity and feeling, dominating the urban hierarchy.
Therefore, option (C) is the correct answer.

chapter: India: People and Economy - Population & Settlements
questionText: Who formulated the mathematical 'Rank-Size Rule' (Pn = P1/n) governing settlement population hierarchies?

options.text: Charles Darwin, in 1859: cities evolve through natural selection
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Albert Einstein, in 1905: cities expand at the speed of light
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Adam Smith, in 1776: city populations are determined by the invisible hand
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

options.text: George Zipf, in 1949: the population of the nth ranked city is 1/n times the population of the largest city
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately solves the problem for Urban Hierarchy Theories.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Urban Hierarchy Theories (India: People and Economy - Population & Settlements):
The Rank-Size Rule was popularized by George Zipf in 1949, stating that the population of the nth ranked city will be 1/n of the population of the largest city in the country (Pn = P1 / n).
Therefore, option (D) is the correct answer.

chapter: India: People and Economy - Population & Settlements
questionText: Which geographers formulated the 'Multiple Nuclei Model' (1945) showing that cities expand around multiple specialized nodes?

options.text: Mark Jefferson (1939), analyzing primate capital cities
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: George Zipf (1949), formulating the rank-size rule
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: C.D. Harris and E.L. Ullman (1945), asserting that modern cities do not grow around a single center but around several distinct specialized nuclei
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT principle for Urban Morphology.

options.text: Ferdinand de Lesseps (1869), designing shipping canals
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for India: People and Economy - Population & Settlements (Urban Morphology):
C.D. Harris and E.L. Ullman (1945), asserting that modern cities do not grow around a single center but around several distinct specialized nuclei

Detailed Analysis:
The Multiple Nuclei Model was developed by Chauncy Harris and Edward Ullman in 1945, showing that large modern cities develop multiple distinct nodes (ports, manufacturing districts, suburban business parks, universities) rather than a single CBD.
Therefore, option (C) is the correct answer.
